executive_summary: On 2020-12-07, observed sessions reached 5,461, representing a 42.0% increase over the 4-weekday baseline of 3,846 sessions. During the same period, the observed purchase rate declined by 14.5% relative to baseline (from 1.95% to 1.67%, a drop of 0.28 percentage points), with an estimated purchase session gap of 15.5 sessions. Financially, performance was positive: recorded purchase revenue reached $8,472.0 USD compared to the baseline of $6,918.0 USD, an absolute increase of $1,554.0 USD (+22.5%). This is confirmed recorded revenue across 110 purchase events with revenue, rather than modeled revenue. Because recorded revenue grew substantially despite the rate dilution, business urgency remains low, warranting routine monitoring rather than emergency intervention.
why_no_alert: No anomaly alert was triggered ('no_qualifying_anomaly'). Although the minimum session count criterion was satisfied (5,461 sessions versus a threshold of 150) and the estimated purchase session gap criterion was satisfied (15.5 versus a threshold of 15), the relative purchase rate decline of -14.5% did not meet the required minimum relative drop threshold of -35%. Because not all anomaly conditions were satisfied, no alert was generated.
